related_questions.question: Is flu A or B worse?

text_blocks.snippet: While both influenza A and B can cause illness, influenza A is generally considered worse. It tends to cause more severe symptoms and outbreaks, and unlike influenza B, it can cause pandemics.
snippet_highlighted_words: influenza A is generally considered worse

list.title: Severity:
list.snippet: Influenza A is often associated with more intense symptoms and can lead to more complications like pneumonia and bronchitis, especially in vulnerable populations.

list.title: Frequency:
list.snippet: Influenza A is generally more common than influenza B.

list.title: Pandemics:
list.snippet: Influenza A is the only type known to cause pandemics, whereas influenza B outbreaks are typically more localized.

list.title: Mutation:
list.snippet: Influenza A viruses mutate more frequently, making it more challenging to develop effective vaccines and potentially contributing to their ability to cause pandemics.

list.title: Severity in children:
list.snippet: While both types can be severe in young children, influenza A is more often linked to ear infections, while influenza B is more associated with seizures, vomiting, and diarrhea in children.

list.title: Timing in flu season:
list.snippet: Influenza A tends to appear earlier in the flu season (fall and early winter) while influenza B tends to occur later (late winter and early spring).
